ch.s: Verses Prologue–9: “These are the hidden sayings that the living Jesus spoke and Didymos Judas Thomas wrote down.”; Verses 10–19: “Jesus said, "I've cast fire on the world, and look, I'm watching over it until it blazes."”; Verses 20–29: “The disciples asked Jesus, "Tell us, what can the kingdom of heaven be compared to?" He said to them, "It can be compared to a mustard seed. Though…”; Verses 30–39: “Jesus said, "Where there are three deities, they're divine. Where there are two or one, I'm with them."”; Verses 40–49: “Jesus said, "A grapevine has been planted outside of the Father. Since it's malnourished, it'll be pulled up by its root and destroyed."”; Verses 50–59: “Jesus said, "If they ask you, 'Where do you come from?' tell them, 'We've come from the light, the place where light came into being by itself, established…”; Verses 60–69: “They saw a Samaritan carrying a lamb to Judea. He said to his disciples, "What do you think he's going to do with that lamb?" They said to…”; Verses 70–79: “Jesus said, "If you give birth to what's within you, what you have within you will save you. If you don't have that within you, what you don't…”; Verses 80–89: “Jesus said, "Whoever has known the world has found the body; but whoever has found the body, of them the world isn't worthy."”; Verses 90–99: “Jesus said, "Come to me, because my yoke is easy and my requirements are light. You'll be refreshed."”; Verses 100–109: “They showed Jesus a gold coin and said to him, "Those who belong to Caesar demand tribute from us." He said to them, "Give to Caesar what belongs…”; Verses 110–114: “Jesus said, "Whoever has found the world and become rich should renounce the world."”. People named: Thomas, John, On, Simon, Peter, Mary. Places: No.
q: Read verses Prologue–9. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 10–19, what do you learn about family and generations?
Read verse 76 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Thomas’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the kingdom of god in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Gospel of Thomas?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Memorize the key verse and come back to it each morning this week.
